architecture_summary.operational_context: Cloud-hosted 3-tier web application serving authenticated users

threat_actors.name: External Opportunistic Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Credential theft, data exfiltration, or defacement for financial gain
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Automated web scanning tools targeting common CVEs on publicly exposed nginx and Flask endpoints
non_capabilities: No physical access to hosting infrastructure
No zero-day budget — limited to public CVEs and common misconfigurations
No insider knowledge of internal network topology

threat_actors.name: Authenticated Insider Threat
threat_actors.motivation: Data exfiltration for personal or competitive gain
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Legitimate application credentials via phishing or credential sharing
non_capabilities: No direct database network access — must go through Flask API
No access to nginx configuration or TLS certificates

attack_paths.impact: Remote code execution on nginx host, pivot to Flask API internal network
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Nginx CVEs require specific versions; opportunistic scanners hit this regularly

attack_paths.impact: SQL injection or SSRF into PostgreSQL from Flask application logic
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Flask apps commonly lack parameterised queries; direct DB access path is high-value

attack_paths.impact: Authenticated access to user data, ability to escalate via application RBAC flaws
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Credential stuffing is highly automated; no MFA assumed on this architecture

attack_paths.entry_point: Flask API executing attacker-controlled SQL via AP-002
attack_paths.impact: Full database dump of user PII and application data
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires successful AP-002; exfil volume limited by query rate and logging

mitigations.control_name: Principle of Least Functionality — nginx hardening
Encrypt or Hash all Authentication Credentials
Network monitoring — anomalous DB query volume

findings.severity_rationale: SQL injection directly into PostgreSQL allows full data dump; no parameterised query controls confirmed in place
No MFA on application login; credential stuffing is automated and highly scalable against this endpoint
Nginx version exposure increases exploitability; patching policy not confirmed
Exfiltration path exists if AP-002 succeeds; no anomaly detection on query volume
